from pysat.solvers import Glucose3
from pysat.card import *

# Langford sequence L(2,15)
# Length 30, positions 0-29
# Each value v (1-15) appears exactly twice, v+1 positions apart
# Fixed: seq[3]=2, seq[11]=14, seq[13]=11, seq[26]=14, seq[27]=7, seq[28]=10

n = 15
length = 30

# Variables: x[v][i] = True means value v is placed at position i
# v in 1..15, i in 0..29
# We'll use variable numbering: var(v, i) = (v-1)*30 + i + 1

def var(v, i):
    return (v-1)*30 + i + 1

solver = Glucose3()

# Constraint 1: Each value v appears exactly twice, at positions i and i+v+1
for v in range(1, n+1):
    # Possible starting positions for value v: 0 to 29-(v+1) = 28-v
    possible_starts = list(range(0, length - v - 1))
    
    # Exactly one starting position must be chosen
    # x[v][i] means value v starts at position i (so also at i+v+1)
    lits = [var(v, i) for i in possible_starts]
    
    # At least one
    solver.add_clause(lits)
    
    # At most one (pairwise)
    for j in range(len(lits)):
        for k in range(j+1, len(lits)):
            solver.add_clause([-lits[j], -lits[k]])

# Constraint 2: Each position has at most one value
for i in range(length):
    lits = [var(v, i) for v in range(1, n+1)]
    # At most one value at position i
    for j in range(len(lits)):
        for k in range(j+1, len(lits)):
            solver.add_clause([-lits[j], -lits[k]])

# Constraint 3: If value v starts at position i, then position i and i+v+1 both have value v
# This is implicit in our encoding - x[v][i] means v is at both i and i+v+1

# Constraint 4: Fixed values
# seq[3] = 2: value 2 is at position 3
# This means either 2 starts at 3 (so also at 6) or 2 starts at 3-2-1=0 (so at 0 and 3)
# Check: if 2 starts at 0, positions are 0 and 3. If 2 starts at 3, positions are 3 and 6.
# So we need: var(2, 0) OR var(2, 3)
solver.add_clause([var(2, 0), var(2, 3)])

# seq[11] = 14: value 14 is at position 11
# 14 starts at 11 (positions 11, 26) or 14 starts at 11-14-1=-4 (invalid)
# So 14 must start at 11
solver.add_clause([var(14, 11)])

# seq[13] = 11: value 11 is at position 13
# 11 starts at 13 (positions 13, 25) or 11 starts at 13-11-1=1 (positions 1, 13)
solver.add_clause([var(11, 1), var(11, 13)])

# seq[26] = 14: value 14 is at position 26
# Already covered by seq[11]=14 (14 starts at 11, so at 11 and 26)

# seq[27] = 7: value 7 is at position 27
# 7 starts at 27 (positions 27, 35 - invalid) or 7 starts at 27-7-1=19 (positions 19, 27)
# So 7 must start at 19
solver.add_clause([var(7, 19)])

# seq[28] = 10: value 10 is at position 28
# 10 starts at 28 (positions 28, 39 - invalid) or 10 starts at 28-10-1=17 (positions 17, 28)
# So 10 must start at 17
solver.add_clause([var(10, 17)])

# Solve
if solver.solve():
    model = solver.get_model()
    seq = [0] * length
    
    for v in range(1, n+1):
        for i in range(length - v - 1):
            if var(v, i) in model:
                seq[i] = v
                seq[i + v + 1] = v
                break
    
    print("Solution found!")
    print(seq)
    
    # Verify
    for v in range(1, n+1):
        positions = [i for i, val in enumerate(seq) if val == v]
        assert len(positions) == 2, f"Value {v} appears {len(positions)} times"
        assert positions[1] - positions[0] == v + 1, f"Value {v} positions {positions} not {v+1} apart"
    
    # Verify fixed values
    assert seq[3] == 2, f"seq[3] = {seq[3]}, expected 2"
    assert seq[11] == 14, f"seq[11] = {seq[11]}, expected 14"
    assert seq[13] == 11, f"seq[13] = {seq[13]}, expected 11"
    assert seq[26] == 14, f"seq[26] = {seq[26]}, expected 14"
    assert seq[27] == 7, f"seq[27] = {seq[27]}, expected 7"
    assert seq[28] == 10, f"seq[28] = {seq[28]}, expected 10"
    
    print("All constraints verified!")
else:
    print("UNSATISFIABLE")

from pysat.solvers import Glucose3

# Langford sequence L(2,15)
# Length 30, positions 0-29
# Each value v (1-15) appears exactly twice, v+1 positions apart
# Fixed: seq[3]=2, seq[11]=14, seq[13]=11, seq[26]=14, seq[27]=7, seq[28]=10

n = 15
length = 30

# Variables: x[v][i] = True means value v starts at position i (occupies i and i+v+1)
# v in 1..15, i in 0..28-v
# Variable numbering: var(v, i) = (v-1)*30 + i + 1

def var(v, i):
    return (v-1)*30 + i + 1

solver = Glucose3()

# Constraint 1: Each value v has exactly one starting position
for v in range(1, n+1):
    possible_starts = list(range(0, length - v - 1))
    lits = [var(v, i) for i in possible_starts]
    
    # Exactly one: at least one + at most one
    solver.add_clause(lits)  # at least one
    for j in range(len(lits)):
        for k in range(j+1, len(lits)):
            solver.add_clause([-lits[j], -lits[k]])  # at most one

# Constraint 2: Each position has exactly one value
# Position i is covered by value v if:
# - v starts at i (first occurrence), or
# - v starts at i-v-1 (second occurrence, i.e., i = start + v + 1)
for i in range(length):
    lits = []
    for v in range(1, n+1):
        # v starts at i (first occurrence at i)
        if i <= length - v - 1:
            lits.append(var(v, i))
        # v starts at i-v-1 (second occurrence at i)
        if i - v - 1 >= 0:
            lits.append(var(v, i - v - 1))
    
    # Exactly one value at position i
    # At least one
    solver.add_clause(lits)
    # At most one (pairwise)
    for j in range(len(lits)):
        for k in range(j+1, len(lits)):

# Constraint 3: Fixed values

solver.add_clause([var(2, 0), var(2, 3)])

solver.add_clause([var(14, 11)])

# seq[13] = 11: position 13 has value 11

solver.add_clause([var(11, 1), var(11, 13)])

# Already covered by var(14, 11)

# seq[27] = 7: position 27 has value 7
# 7 starts at 27 (positions 27,35 - invalid) or 7 starts at 19 (positions 19,27)
solver.add_clause([var(7, 19)])

# seq[28] = 10: position 28 has value 10
# 10 starts at 28 (positions 28,39 - invalid) or 10 starts at 17 (positions 17,28)
solver.add_clause([var(10, 17)])

# Solve
if solver.solve():

    seq = [0] * length

    assert seq[11] == 14, f"seq[11] = {seq[11]}, expected 14"
